quarterly_data.signal: OCS ahead of plan (CEO Michael Hurlston): the OCS business is 'exceeding internal expectations' - Lumentum had targeted its first $10 million OCS quarter for fiscal Q3 and 'cleared that bar three months ahead of schedule.' OCS order backlog 'now has surged well past $400 million, the majority of which is slated for shipment in the second half of this calendar year' (repeated in Q&A as 'primarily deliverable in the back half of the year', although one Q&A answer said 'most of which is going to be shipped in 2027'). The backlog comes from three customers ('It's three customers making up that backlog'), each increasing demand, and deliveries to all three were accelerated this quarter. The calendar Q4 OCS exit previously pegged at around $100 million 'looks like it'll be quite a bit higher than that'; the 2027 run rate is expected to step up again. Lumentum did not split the $400 million between the two quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: first $10 million OCS quarter reached three months early; OCS backlog well past $400 million (three customers); calendar Q4 exit above the prior around $100 million view

quarterly_data.signal: OCS applications (Wupen Yuen, President, Global Business Units): no change to the four dominant OCS use cases - spine replacement, scale-across applications, optical scale-up, and protection/redundancy in the network. All OCS customers use these applications to different degrees; other scenarios may emerge and are being watched, but 'these four, to us today, they're the dominant application scenarios.'
quarterly_data.figure: four dominant OCS applications: spine replacement, scale-across, optical scale-up, protection/redundancy

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q2 2026 results (quarter ended December 27, 2025; non-GAAP): record revenue of $665.5 million, at the high end of guidance, with over 65% year-over-year growth - a company record for the second reporting period in a row. Non-GAAP gross margin 42.5% (up 310 basis points sequentially, 820 basis points year-on-year on utilization, increased pricing on select products and mix led by data center laser chips); non-GAAP operating margin 25.2% (up 1,730 basis points year-on-year); non-GAAP EPS $1.67; GAAP net income $78.2 million. Components revenue $443.7 million (up 17% sequentially, 68% year-on-year) on laser chips, laser assemblies and inline subsystems; Systems revenue $221.8 million (up 43% sequentially, 60% year-on-year). Pump laser revenue grew over 90% year-over-year to a record, and narrow linewidth laser assembly shipments grew for the eighth consecutive quarter; industrial end-market shipments were roughly flat sequentially. CapEx was $84 million, primarily for cloud and AI manufacturing capacity; cash and short-term investments rose to $1.16 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $665.5 million (over 65% YoY); non-GAAP gross margin 42.5%; operating margin 25.2%; EPS $1.67; Components $443.7 million (+68%); Systems $221.8 million (+60%); pump lasers over 90% YoY; CapEx $84 million

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 2026 guidance (CFO Wajid Ali, non-GAAP): net revenue $780 to $830 million; the $805 million midpoint would be a new all-time quarterly record and 'represents an impressive 85% plus year-over-year increase' (CEO). Operating margin 30% to 31%; diluted EPS $2.15 to $2.35; tax rate 16.5%; approximately 92 million shares. Lumentum had previously projected crossing $750 million of quarterly revenue by mid-2026 and now expects to 'comfortably surpass that milestone next quarter.' About two-thirds of the sequential increase is expected from components (cloud applications) and one-third from systems (high-speed transceivers and OCS). Price increases start flowing through in the March guide; the CEO called the effect 'relatively modest.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 FY2026 guide $780 to $830 million ($805 million midpoint, 85% plus YoY); operating margin 30% to 31%; EPS $2.15 to $2.35

quarterly_data.signal: CPO / ultra-high-power (UHP) lasers: Lumentum 'secured an additional multi-$100 million purchase order for ultra-high-power lasers that support optical scale-out applications,' with shipments for this order in 2027 ('clicking in in the first half of 2027'). Initial CPO orders remain on track for a material UHP shipment inflection in the second half of calendar 2026, pegged at 'somewhere around $50 million in the fourth calendar quarter. Perhaps more.' The ramp spans multiple customers and is hitting faster than forecast last quarter: 'We're very much sold out in our powered laser fab.' Hurlston cited the 400 milliwatts power level ('not something that many people can do') and reliability proven in subsea applications as the basis for broader CPO customer engagement.
quarterly_data.figure: additional multi-$100 million UHP laser purchase order (shipments first half of 2027); around $50 million UHP/CPO revenue in the fourth calendar quarter; 400 milliwatts lasers

quarterly_data.signal: New growth vectors: Lumentum has 'a clear line of sight into the broader external light source (ELS) market' - pluggable ELS modules rather than standalone laser chips - which Hurlston sized at 'somewhere around two, two and a half times content gain from a revenue standpoint as compared to just our lasers,' at decent margins, and which diversifies the customer base as new partners adopt next-generation scale-out architectures. Optical scale-up is named a fourth growth driver: 'By late calendar 2027, we would expect our first scale-up CPO shipments replacing longer copper connections,' with Lumentum in design-in cycles using UHP lasers and ELS modules. Yuen called scale-up 'a brand new market that didn't exist before.' Given the scale-up opportunity, Lumentum is 'in active negotiations with leading customers to offset our capital requirements in exchange for long-term supply assurances.'
quarterly_data.figure: ELS module around two, two and a half times content gain vs lasers alone; first scale-up CPO shipments by late calendar 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: the indium phosphide wafer fab capacity 'remains at a premium, fully allocated.' Lumentum front-loaded its 40% expansion target (all at Sagamihara), delivering 'a little bit north of 20% in the December alone,' with 'another 20% to go over the next couple of quarters' and likely a little better than 40% overall. It now has line of sight to further capacity through the second half of calendar 2026 into early 2027 via Sagamihara, the Caswell, United Kingdom fab and the second Japan fab at Takao. Management said new fab capacity 'by, you know, acquisition or something of that nature' is an active investigation. Back-end factory capacity is also a significant constraint: Lumentum has 'pivoted from a manufacturing strategy to really look at more contract manufacturing,' is stepping up its Nava, Thailand site, clearing some China factory footprint for the most important SKUs, and hired a new back-end operations leader (from Jabil) to move more products to contract manufacturers.
quarterly_data.figure: 40% InP capacity expansion front-loaded (north of 20% in the December quarter; another 20% over the next couple of quarters); more capacity from Sagamihara, Caswell and Takao

quarterly_data.signal: Supply-demand imbalance and LTAs: even after adding 20% capacity the imbalance is 'about the same this quarter as last quarter' ('If anything, it's incrementally up'), 'roughly 25 to 30%' - 'We're undershipping our customers' demand by somewhere around 30%.' Hurlston: 'All of our capacity, just to be very clear on EML, is spoken for in these LTAs. We have very tight LTAs that run through the balance of calendar 2027,' with pricing leeway and 'a couple of step-ups' already done. CFO Ali: prices 'are holding or they're increasing'; customers are asking for more than their LTA volumes, allowing incremental pricing on those units, and customers that will not sign an LTA get only what is left after committed partners are allocated. LTAs are also being pushed into telecom products, where a couple of key customers have been 'problematic' and Lumentum sees more room to raise prices.
quarterly_data.figure: undershipping customer demand by somewhere around 30% (roughly 25 to 30%); EML capacity fully committed under LTAs through calendar 2027

quarterly_data.signal: EML / lane-speed mix: another quarterly record in EML laser shipments, led by 100 gig lane speeds and bolstered by a ramp in 200 gig devices; 200 gig devices were 'approximately 5% of unit volume' but 'roughly 10% of data center laser chip revenue' (roughly two to one pricing), reached a quarter earlier than expected because 1.6T is arriving faster. Lumentum expects 200 gig to be 25% of its mix by the end of the calendar year and is introducing 200 gig differential EMLs as a further ASP and margin tailwind. 'Most of the initial transceivers that are going to 1.6T are based on EMLs'; management still expects silicon photonics to be the majority of 1.6T transceiver shipments (EML dominant in WDM-based architectures, silicon photonics gaining in parallel fiber), yet the absolute number of Lumentum EMLs 'will go up for us and rather appreciably.' Lumentum also shipped CW lasers to 800 gig manufacturers and increased UHP laser shipments for CPO.
quarterly_data.figure: 200 gig approximately 5% of unit volume, roughly 10% of data center laser chip revenue; 200 gig expected at 25% of mix by end of calendar year

quarterly_data.signal: Cloud transceivers: systems growth was led by cloud transceivers, 'increasing by approximately $50 million on the quarter' on expanded manufacturing capacity in Thailand; transceiver revenue outperformed the legacy run rate and is guided up again in Q3. Lumentum is 'now in the lead pack of transceiver suppliers' for the 1.6T transition, and 1.6T is 'definitely stronger' than ninety days earlier with a couple of large customers pushing deliveries. Having earlier talked of managing transceivers to about $250 million a quarter or a billion dollars, management now says capping it there will be 'more difficult,' with demand from the primary customer and others; CFO Ali said 1.6T margins are 'significantly better than 800G,' though transceivers remain a margin headwind. The in-house CW laser plus own-transceiver introduction slipped 'a two to three-month push out' to late Q2, early Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: cloud transceivers up approximately $50 million QoQ; transceiver business might be greater than a billion dollars (earlier $250 million a quarter / a billion dollars framing); in-house CW transceiver launch pushed two to three months
